23/S0.subgoal: Explain the motivation for treating XR systems as interactive systems and describe the disappearing-technology ideal, relating it to presence and historical computing trends.

23/S1.subgoal: Explain that interactive systems involve lay users and why designers should avoid forcing users to learn the underlying technology.

23/S2.subgoal: Describe the user-centric approach to designing interactive systems.

23/S3.subgoal: Define human-computer interaction and identify its core concern as incorporating humans into design.

23/S4.subgoal: Explain why human factors require knowing user characteristics, using a railway ticket-booking example to show that different users need different interfaces.

23/S5.subgoal: Summarize the main points of the lecture and preview the next part.

goal.goal: Explain why XR systems are interactive systems and how user-centric, human-factors principles guide their design for lay users.
goal.achieves: Prepares the learner to incorporate human factors and user-centered design into later understanding, development, and evaluation of XR systems.

objectives.goal: Explain why XR systems should be treated as interactive systems and how the disappearing-technology ideal supports presence and design for lay users.
objectives.achieves: Gives the learner a rationale for making XR technology unobtrusive and usable by non-experts before applying human-factors design in later XR development.

objectives.goal: Describe the human-centered design framework for interactive XR systems by connecting the user-centric approach, HCI, and human factors to user characteristics.
objectives.achieves: Enables the learner to consider user characteristics and human factors when designing or evaluating XR interfaces in the course case study.
